text: Working with APIs is a common task for developers. An API allows your program to communicate with another service, usually by sending HTTP requests. Most APIs return data in JSON format, which is easy to read and use. Before you can access an API, you often need authentication, such as an API key, to prove who you are. APIs also have rate limits, meaning you can only send a certain number of requests in a given time. Finally, good error handling is important, because things can go wrong, and your program should respond to problems gracefully.
